_comment: Bakersfield-Delano, CA MSA — Kern County. Ingested from the ChatGPT Work research workbook 2026-08-03 as part of wave 1 of the v2.0 methodology. NOT YET IMPORTED. `expected_publish` is deliberately ABSENT: for a new metro the projected split IS the finding the owner needs, so it is reported by --stage=project rather than asserted. Once the owner approves the split, record it here so the real import run re-asserts it.
_workbook_comment: FIRST WAVE UNDER RESEARCH METHODOLOGY v2.0, AND THE TAB OVERRIDE IS LOAD-BEARING. v2.0 splits the human research artifact from the machine handoff: the 15 human tabs are unchanged and a new generated `Import Contract` tab is now the ONLY machine input. This workbook is generation A by tab layout, so detectGeneration() picks generation A and would read its default primary tab `Import Ready` — which v2.0 demotes to 'a human-readable view of what is proposed for import'. Reading a human tab as machine input is exactly the Huntsville defect class (a per-row simulation log read as the venue table, silently yielding 30 address-less venues). So the primary tab is pinned explicitly. applyTabOverrides() ABORTS if the named tab is missing rather than falling back silently, which is what makes this safe to pin. `venues` and `evidence` keep their generation-A defaults.
_envelope_comment: Derived from the MSA COUNTY LIST, not the observed venue bbox (Toledo precedent) — the observed bbox is only a LOWER bound and an envelope cut to it would reject a legitimate future venue near the metro edge. The Bakersfield-Delano MSA is coextensive with Kern County, so the envelope is Kern County's own extent, rounded OUTWARD to 0.01 deg. Extent taken from the US Census TIGERweb State_County service (authoritative for US county geography) rather than Nominatim, whose request budget is reserved for venue geocoding. Kern County: lat 34.788655..35.798392, lng -120.194369..-117.616517. Kern is a large land county with no significant water over-extension, so this is a straightforward case — no Ottawa-County water caveat applies.
_exclude_comment: OWNER RULING 2026-08-05, consistent with the McAllen precedent. Both rows would have PUBLISHED under the coverage-first gate carrying NO source URL of any kind — not a weak citation, none. Their only evidence was playtimescheduler.com, which workbook-extract correctly strips from the user-facing columns (AGGREGATOR_HOST), leaving website and name_source_url both null. A venue page with nothing to cite is not what verification_status='listed' means under ADR-18. Both are also private/HOA, so a visiting player likely cannot use them, and each row's own public_notes already says to confirm before visiting. EXCLUDED rather than held: exclude removes them from the run entirely, so no candidate row, no listing row, and any future re-research starts clean. The research is not lost — it stays in the artifact and the reason is recorded here. expected_count drops 20 -> 18 accordingly, because an excluded venue is not counted toward it.

exclude.reason: Would publish with no source URL at all (aggregator-only evidence, stripped by ADR-14). access_type='private'. Owner ruling 2026-08-05 — McAllen precedent.

Would publish with no source URL at all (aggregator-only evidence, stripped by ADR-14). access_type='hoa'; the row's own note says 'appears residential; access rules and controlling-entity confirmation remain open'. Owner ruling 2026-08-05 — McAllen precedent.

_geocode_comment: 17 of 20 venues geocoded (15 high precision, 2 low). THE THREE MISSES WERE INVESTIGATED, not waved through. dignity-health-sports-complex-gsa carries a suite address ('3101 Gilmore Avenue #100') that misses every rung. bear-valley-springs is the interesting one: its street locus 'Rolling Oak Drive' resolved 465 km from the venue's own zip centroid, so the township guard correctly DISCARDED it rather than publishing a coordinate 465 km wrong — the guard doing exactly its job. natatorium-courts has an intersection, not an address ('4th Street and Warren Street'), which no rung can resolve. The two low-precision rows (mesa-marin, riverview) anchored to a highway and to the wrong residential street respectively — repair-pass class 1a, needing a better ANCHOR rather than a better address. Every miss is a genuine HTTP 200 with an empty result set, not rate limiting: scripts/lib/geocode-nominatim.mjs throws on any non-200, so an empty result cannot be a masked failure. Set false so these import as gate-blocked drafts in the work queue (the Little Rock precedent) instead of aborting the metro; the publish gate holds each on 'no coordinate'.
_expected_publish_comment: RE-AUTHORED 2026-08-05 from the confirming --stage=project run under the CURRENT gate, approved by the owner. The previous block (count 11) was locked 2026-08-03 against the pre-ADR-16/17 gate, which held rows on coordinate precision 'low' and on research_status != 'verified' — both retired, so every reason string in it was stale. It was REPLACED, not edited to match output: the block was removed, the projection was run with no expectation present, and this was written from what it printed. riverview is held on research_status='held' rather than excluded because the VENUE is fine and only the COORDINATE is wrong — the cached geocode for '401 Willow Drive / 93308' returned OSM way/10436658 named 'Willow Creek Drive' as a road centroid with no house number, the name-qualified query returned [], and OSM has no Willow Drive in 93308 at all (the one that exists is 5.3 km east in 93301). This config's own _geocode_comment already described it as anchored to 'the wrong residential street'. Holding keeps the row in the work queue so a re-geocode releases it; exclude would drop it from the batch. That distinction is the pattern: real-venue-bad-coordinate holds, not-a-venue excludes.
